title: Determination of orthodontic bracket and tooth adaptation using an X-ray micro-computer tomography scanner
author: Fakir, Keanly, et al.
materials: -Orthodontic brackets-Plaster/gypsum / previously removed teeth-Industrial or medical X-ray micro-computer tomography scanner-Processing software for the analysis, in this method Volume graphics VG Studio max 3.2.5 (Heidelberg, Germany 2018).

The method here is described for the use with an industrial Nikon Metrology XTH 225 ST X-ray micro-computer tomography scanner (Yokohama, Japan) and Volume graphics VG Studio max 3.2.5, but any X-ray micro-computer tomography scanner and software for analysis can be used for image acquisition and analysis.

steps.title: Gather equipment and software
steps.instruction: Collect orthodontic brackets, plaster/gypsum models with previously removed maxillary second premolars, a firm foam holder, an industrial or medical X‑ray micro‑CT scanner (e.g., Nikon Metrology XTH 225 ST), and the analysis software VolumeGraphics VG Studio Max 3.2.5 (or equivalent).

steps.title: Prepare teeth specimens
steps.instruction: Select a maxillary second premolar from each model, trim the surrounding model away so only the tooth remains, assign a unique identification number to each tooth, and mount the teeth in batches of three on a firm foam holder.

steps.title: Scan specimens with micro‑CT
steps.instruction: Place each batch of three teeth (and the corresponding brackets) in the X‑ray micro‑CT scanner. Scan each batch for 50 min using 2984 projections, with no detector shift. Apply copper filtration of 0.25 mm for teeth and 1 mm for brackets. Use 100 kV tube voltage, 200 µA beam current, and an exposure of 1 fps. Set voxel size to 20 µm for teeth scans and 4.99 µm for bracket scans. No beam‑hardening correction is required for the tooth scans. Scan brackets three or four at a time, then separate them for individual analysis.

steps.title: Export raw volumes to VG Studio
steps.instruction: In VG Studio Max 3.2.5, use the selection mode to crop the contour of each tooth and each bracket, export each cropped region as a raw volume, and transfer the raw data files to the analysis workstation. No segmentation is performed because internal structures are not required.

steps.title: Measure bracket height and width
steps.instruction: Open each bracket raw volume in VG Studio and measure its overall height and width. Record the values: Bioquick (Forestadent) 3.07 mm × 3.45 mm; Innovation (GAC) 3.25 mm × 4.46 mm; Victory series (3 M Unitek) 2.88 mm × 3.29 mm.

steps.title: Calculate standardized contact offsets
steps.instruction: Define the standardized area of contact as 75 % of the bracket height and width. Compute vertical offset = 0.75 × (height / 2) and horizontal offset = 0.75 × (width / 2) for each bracket. Resulting offsets: Victory series – vertical 1.08 mm, horizontal 1.23 mm; Innovation – vertical 1.21 mm, horizontal 1.30 mm; Bioquick – vertical 1.15 mm, horizontal 1.30 mm.

steps.title: Locate bracket centre (target point)
steps.instruction: In the bracket volume, locate the centre point at the intersection of half the measured width and half the measured height. Place a landmark at this centre and record its x, y, z coordinates (the “target point of the bracket”).

steps.title: Create bracket landmark points A‑B‑C
steps.instruction: Using the target‑point coordinates and the offsets calculated in step 5, place three additional landmarks on the bracket: Point A (inferior mesial) at X_target + horizontal_offset, Y_target − vertical_offset; Point B (gingival mesial) at X_target + horizontal_offset, Y_target + vertical_offset; Point C (gingival distal) at X_target − horizontal_offset, Y_target + vertical_offset. Record the x, y, z coordinates for each point.

steps.title: Determine bracket curvature and angles
steps.instruction:
For the mesial curve (A‑B) and the gingival curve (B‑C):
1. Measure the curve length with the VG Studio measuring tool.
2. Locate the midpoint of each curve.
3. Place an additional landmark midway between the midpoint and each endpoint, giving five points per curve.
4. Fit a best‑fitting circle through the five points using the circle tool; the software automatically defines the circle origin.
5. Draw radii from the origin to the two original endpoints of the curve.
6. Measure the angle between the two radii (in degrees) for the mesial and for the gingival curve.
7. Record all radii lengths and angles in an Excel spreadsheet.

steps.title: Measure tooth dimensions and axis
steps.instruction: In the tooth volume, measure the total width from one contact point to the opposite contact point. Use this width together with the cusp tip to define the central longitudinal axis of the tooth. Place a target point on this axis 4 mm apical to the cusp tip and record its x, y, z coordinates.

steps.title: Place bracket landmarks on tooth coordinates
steps.instruction: Using the tooth target point and the bracket vertical/horizontal offsets (from step 5), calculate the tooth‑surface coordinates for points A, B, and C for each bracket type (as shown in Table 3). Plot these three points on the tooth surface to define the mesial and gingival regions where the bracket will contact the tooth.

steps.title: Determine tooth curvature and angles
steps.instruction:
For each tooth‑surface curve (mesial A‑B and gingival B‑C):
1. Slice the tooth volume at the three landmark points to isolate the curve.
2. Measure the curve length and place a midpoint landmark.
3. Add two additional landmarks: one midway between the midpoint and point A, another midway between the midpoint and point B (for the mesial curve) or point C (for the gingival curve), yielding five points total.
4. Fit a best‑fitting circle through the five points with the circle tool; the origin is placed automatically.
5. Draw radii from the origin to the two original endpoints of the curve.
6. Measure the angle between the radii (central angle) and record it in the Excel sheet.
7. Repeat for the gingival curve.

steps.title: Compare bracket and tooth curvature angles
steps.instruction: Transfer all mesial and gingival angle measurements for the three brackets and the corresponding tooth curves into a single Excel spreadsheet. Compare each bracket’s mesial and gingival angles with the tooth’s mesial and gingival angles to identify which bracket curvature most closely matches the tooth curvature.
